title: ОСОБЕ СА ИСКУСТВОМ ЖИВОТА У БЕСКУЋНИШТВУ КАО КОРИСНИЦИ БИБЛИОТЕЧКИХ УСЛУГА: СТАВОВИ И ИСКУСТВА БИБЛИОТЕКАРА
abstract: Summary This paper presents the results of a study conducted through a series of interactive professional seminars held during 2026 in several public libraries and the National Library of Serbia, focusing on the provision of library services for people experiencing homelessness. The broader context of the study encompassed issues of inclusive librarianship, understanding the needs of library users with specific needs, familiarity with the legal framework that supports the implementation of the equal rights agenda for all, and the application of international recommendations that facilitate more effective work by librarians with members of vulnerable social groups. An analysis of librarians’ attitudes toward library services for people experiencing homelessness, as well as an overview of the current state of inclusive librarianship in Serbian libraries, was based on a survey conducted during the seminars. The survey findings also served as a basis for defining recommended measures aimed at achieving best practices in this field. The paper describes the main topics, objectives, and conclusions of the seminars, with the intention of promoting this research model as applicable to other contemporary issues of importance to librarianship at the national level. The primary aim of this paper is to draw the attention of the professional community to the complex social issue of homelessness, which requires a comprehensive approach in which libraries play a highly significant role.
affiliations: Ana Savić; Dobrila Begenišić

title: УНИВЕРЗИТЕТСКА БИБЛИОТЕКА И ПОДРШКА ДОКТОРСКИМ СТУДИЈАМА: РАД НА ДОДАТНОМ ОБРАЗОВАЊУ МЛАЂИХ ИСТРАЖИВАЧА
abstract: Summary This paper presents a range of activities carried out by the University Library “Svetozar Marković” that are related to doctoral dissertations and doctoral studies. It provides an overview of educational programs and other information services that were ultimately consolidated and systematized in 2022 through the establishment of the Centre for Doctoral Studies Support (CDSS). The founding of the Centre marked a key milestone, not only in bringing together existing activities related to doctoral studies but also as an important prerequisite for their further development. In the years that followed, with the support of the Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation of the Republic of Serbia, the Centre launched an extensive educational program comprising seminars, presentations, and workshops on topics important to scientific research. By mid-2026, the program had engaged dozens of distinguished lecturers and attracted several thousand participants. In addition to cooperating with partner institutions—centers affiliated with university libraries at other universities in Serbia—the CDSS seeks to strengthen its communication with doctoral students to ensure the continuous evaluation and improvement of its work. All activities are carried out with the aim of fulfilling the Centre’s mission: to enhance the research activities of higher education institutions by assisting members of the academic community who are at the very beginning of their scientific careers.

title: ВИШЕ ОД ПРОНАЛАЖЕЊА ИНФОРМАЦИЈА: КОРИСНИЦИ И УСЛУГЕ ОДЕЉЕЊА ЗА НАУЧНЕ ИНФОРМАЦИЈЕ НАРОДНЕ БИБЛИОТЕКЕ СРБИЈЕ
abstract: Summary In 2001, the Department of Scientific Information of the National Library of Serbia initiated the establishment of KoBSON (Consortium of Libraries of Serbia for Unified Acquisition), intending to optimize the acquisition of foreign scientific information, transitioning from print to electronic publications, improving access to electronic resources, and promoting domestic scientific publishing. Today, 25 years after KoBSON’s founding, the Department’s activities remain focused on achieving and advancing these original goals. This paper provides an overview of their realization through a presentation of the most frequently used services that the Department offers to researchers in Serbia. Additionally, the paper describes the collaboration in providing assistance and support to scientific publishing in Serbia.

title: AWARENESS AND ATTITUDE OF LIBRARIANS TOWARD ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR EFFECTIVE SERVICE DELIVERY IN UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES IN TARABA STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: University libraries are expected to provide fast, accurate, and technology-driven information services to support students, researchers, and academic staff. Although artificial intelligence (AI) tools can enhance cataloguing, reference services, and information retrieval, service delivery in many university libraries in Taraba State remains predominantly manual. Preliminary observations also indicate gaps in librarians’ awareness and attitudes toward AI, yet the extent to which these factors influence service delivery is unclear. This study examined librarians’ awareness and attitudes toward AI tools and their effect on information service delivery in university libraries in Taraba State. A descriptive survey design was adopted, involving 122 librarians from Federal University Wukari (FUW), Taraba State University (TSU) Jalingo, and Kwararafa University Wukari (KUW). Data from 117 valid questionnaires were analyzed using descriptive statistics and one-way ANOVA at the 0.05 significance level. Results showed a high level of AI awareness among librarians (overall mean = 4.19), with KUW exhibiting the highest consistency, followed by TSU and FUW. Attitudes toward AI were also strongly positive across all institutions (overall mean = 4.41). ANOVA revealed significant institutional differences in awareness (p = .000 < .05) and attitudes (p = .002 < .05), attributed to variations in training, exposure, and institutional support. The study concludes that librarians’ AI awareness and attitudes significantly shape the efficiency and quality of information service delivery. It recommends targeted AI training programmes, enhanced institutional support, and clear policy frameworks to strengthen AI adoption in university libraries in Taraba State.
affiliations: YAKUBU, Ande Sarki (CLN, MNLA); Israel Habibu. PhD. (CLN) IDRIS

title: Which reported inputs govern molecular docking reproducibility? A benchmark from reporting audit to independent re-execution
abstract:
arXiv:2609.37542v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computational docking results can be re-executed only when the molecular system and protocol are specified, yet reporting checklists do not quantify how strongly individual method fields affect the reported score. We combined a span-verified audit of 50 open-access papers with controlled one-factor perturbations, a Vinardo scoring-function check and a Vina cross-docking extension covering 12 targets in 7 protein families, and re-execution of 37 published claims on local and independent cloud infrastructure. Search-related fields were sparsely reported, but perturbing box centre, box size, exhaustiveness or random seed produced median absolute score changes of no more than 0.08 kcal mol$^{-1}$; ligand protonation and identity produced median changes of 0.19 and 0.29 kcal mol$^{-1}$, respectively, whereas receptor structure produced the largest change (1.02 kcal mol$^{-1}$; n = 85; P < 0.001), and 22% of 116 unique reported ligand strings remained unresolved or ambiguous after deterministic name normalization. These measurements yielded empirical field weights for the NewScience Evidence score and identified exact receptor structure, machine-resolvable ligand identity and protonation state as primary reporting elements; 29 of 37 local and 27 of 37 cloud re-executions were within 2.0 kcal mol$^{-1}$ of the reported score, but these descriptive rates do not estimate experimental replication or a calibrated probability of reproduction.
thinking: 该研究通过系统审计和独立复现，量化了分子对接计算中不同输入参数对结果可重复性的影响，方法严谨且具有实证基础。其发现直接指向科学计算报告规范的改进，对计算化学和数字图书馆中的科学数据管理具有明确的实践价值，但技术本身属于计算化学的经典方法，前沿性有限。

title: The Preprint Evolution: The Rise of Unreviewed Drafts on arXiv and its Implications for Astronomy
abstract:
arXiv:2609.35787v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: The arXiv preprint server originally democratized astronomical research by digitizing the circulation of early manuscripts and removing the financial barriers of journal subscriptions. However, a system designed for the lower publication volumes of the 1990s has fractured under modern research output. Today, the sheer volume of unreviewed manuscripts---often tagged as ``submitted,'', ``under review'', or ``comments welcome''---imposes a severe cognitive ``tax'' on the community. Researchers are forced to track multiple, unvetted versions of the same work, creating a massive redundant workload. This practice also bypasses the blinded peer-review process by establishing premature precedence, and it takes a heavy toll on early-career researchers. The pressure to rapidly post unvetted results stifles independent research, pushing young scientists toward massive mainstream collaborations where individual creativity gets lost. In this Short Communication, I analyze a decade of astro-ph metadata to quantify this trend. To safeguard both researchers' time and research freedom, I propose bifurcating submissions into two separate streams. Level-1 (peer-reviewed science) would host peer-reviewed science (accompanied by a journal acceptance or final DOI), while Level-2 (pre-review drafts) would be reserved for discussion drafts. This distinction would remove the unfair advantage of establishing false precedence through drafts and drastically cut the daily reading burden by allowing researchers to opt out of tracking unvetted versions.
thinking: 论文通过分析arXiv天文领域十年元数据，量化了未经同行评审预印本激增带来的问题，方法严谨且数据支撑充分。其提出的分级提交方案具有明确的实践指导意义，但技术层面未涉及前沿算法或模型，属于对现有系统的优化建议。
one_sentence_summary: 该研究指出arXiv上未经评审的预印本泛滥增加了科研人员负担，并提出了将提交内容分为已评审和讨论稿两级的解决方案。

title: The Uneven Decline of Collective Knowledge Production: Evidence from Stack Overflow After Generative AI
abstract:
arXiv:2609.36069v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Generative AI (Gen AI) is reshaping how individuals learn and work, but its consequences for collective knowledge, the shared body of knowledge that online communities produce together, remain poorly understood. Prior work has documented an aggregate decline in participation on knowledge-sharing platforms, but it remains unclear which specific kinds of knowledge are being lost first. We study this question using Stack Overflow, one of the largest online communities for software engineering, treating the release of ChatGPT-3.5 as a natural shock. Analyzing over two million questions posted between 2020 and 2025, we track how two dimensions of collective knowledge, difficulty and data availability, change following Gen AI's release. Using diverse methods and robust checks, we find consistent patterns. Easy questions decline sharply while difficult questions become more common, a pattern corroborated by rising code complexity. Data-rich topics and tags lose share of questions, while data-scarce ones gain ground. The two dimensions also interact: the decline in easy questions is concentrated specifically within data-rich domains, while difficult questions increase regardless of data availability. This pattern extends beyond Python across programming languages, with more prevalent languages showing sharper shifts. Together, our findings reveal that Gen AI's impact on collective knowledge is uneven, eroding easy, accessible knowledge first while more complex, less common knowledge persists.
thinking: 该论文采用双重差分法，将ChatGPT发布作为自然实验，方法设计严谨，因果推断逻辑清晰。研究聚焦生成式AI对集体知识生产的结构性影响，选题前沿且具有现实意义，但结论主要基于Stack Overflow单一平台，外部效度有待进一步验证。
one_sentence_summary: 研究发现，生成式AI导致Stack Overflow上简单、数据丰富的问题大幅减少，而复杂、数据稀缺的问题相对增加，揭示了AI对集体知识生产的非均衡影响。

title: Generating Synthetic Citation Networks with Communities
abstract:
arXiv:2604.25597v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Generating realistic synthetic citation, patent, or component dependency networks is essential for benchmarking community detection, graph visualisation, and network data mining algorithms. We present a systematic comparison of generators of directed graphs that are nearly acyclic and have a ground-truth community structure. We evaluate 12 methods across 7 real citation networks and 26 metrics. We propose the practice of reversing the directions of edges in static generators to break cycles and induce a citation-like flow, which markedly improves the performance of a degree-corrected Stochastic Block Model. Our methodological approach to evaluating community detection benchmarks distinguishes between endogenous and exogenous mesoscopic similarities, with the latter proving more important. This distinction reveals that high-parameter models gain much of their advantage by memorising planted community statistics, which limits their fidelity when the evaluation is blind to those labels. Finally, we introduce the Citation Seeder (CS) algorithm, an iterative generator grounded in the Price-Pareto model of citation networks, with interpretable parameters and O(N+E) generation. CS achieves competitive results against the best-performing baselines while using up to four orders of magnitude fewer parameters, providing an interpretable account of a network's structure and, on a temporal hold-out, extrapolating its future in-degree distribution more faithfully than descriptive baselines.
thinking: 论文系统比较了12种有向图生成方法在7个真实引文网络上的表现，并提出了改进现有模型和评估基准的新方法，方法严谨且实验设计系统。其核心贡献在于引入了可解释性强、参数极少的Citation Seeder算法，但研究更侧重于为社区检测等算法提供基准测试工具，其直接解决图书馆或信息机构具体业务问题的实践路径尚不明确。
one_sentence_summary: 该研究提出了一种参数极少、可解释性强的引文网络生成算法，为社区检测等图算法的基准测试提供了更优的工具。

title: X-DigCheck: Co-Evolving Application Profiles and Knowledge Graphs, Demonstrated on the RTI Documentation of Rupe Magna
abstract:
arXiv:2609.07694v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We demonstrate X-DigCheck, a domain-independent environment for building and maintaining application profiles as they co-evolve with the data they describe. Profiles developed against a fixed ontology quickly drift from the schema they were meant to capture. X-DigCheck treats profile construction as a continuous ontology-data co-evolution loop: data are lifted into RDF against the profile, checked through competency questions and SHACL, and the resulting reports jointly drive revisions of the ontology, mappings, constraints, and graph. The loop is agnostic to the domain and to the pipeline that produces the graph. We validate and demonstrate the tool in the cultural heritage domain, on the construction of RupeMagna-RTI, the first Reflectance Transformation Imaging (RTI) specialisation of the Cultural Heritage Survey ODP (CHS-ODP), aligned with CIDOC-CRM/CRMdig, ArCo, CHAD-KG, and Getty AAT, with semRTI as the lifting pipeline of this use case. The demonstration lets visitors run one full turn of the loop -on the shipped Rupe Magna (Grosio, Italy) RTI survey, or on a profile and graph of their own -executing the competency-question and SHACL checks live and reading the bidirectional coverage report that flags modelling gaps and stale assumptions. The result is a portable co-evolution environment for profile engineering, together with a reusable RTI application profile produced through it. A screencast of the demonstration is available at https://zenodo.org/records/22210609.
thinking: 论文提出了一种支持应用规范与知识图谱协同演化的工具X-DigCheck，其核心方法——基于能力问题和SHACL约束的持续验证与反馈循环——在知识组织领域具有方法学上的前沿性和严谨性。研究在文化遗产领域的RTI数据上进行了具体验证，并产出了可复用的应用规范，具有明确的实践价值，但工具本身的普适性验证和在不同领域的落地效果仍有待更多案例证明。
